items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: As often as he played – I was standing in the back – I forget what the performance was – with Bobby Hackett.

ctx.x: . . . by Joe Glaser, yeah. But he never lost that joy. As often as he played – I was standing in the back – I forget what the performance was – with Bobby Hackett. He was playing When it’s Sleepy Time down South. Bobby almost had tears in his eyes. He said, “Do you hear that? He stays with the melody, and yet it becomes something else.” That was part of that magic he had. It’s hard to put into words.
Going back to your days in Boston and these musicians, Vic Dickenson and Edmund Hall and all them – was Ken Kersey there also?
